templates.name: Kinetic enolate formation
templates.provenance: Ported from original MolecularReactivityEngine.execute_first_principles_step pathway A. Chemistry: Fleming, I. 'Molecular Orbitals and Organic Chemical Reactions' (2010). Strong hindered bases (LDA, t-BuOK) deprotonate the alpha-carbon to give the enolate; branching over all alpha positions shows both kinetic and thermodynamic isomers. Restricted to aldehyde/ketone carbonyls (acids/esters/amides excluded — their O-H or N-H chemistry dominates) and alpha-carbons that actually bear an H.

templates.name: E2 beta-elimination (HBr)
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. 'A Collection of Robust Organic Synthesis Reactions for In Silico Molecule Design' J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Anti-periplanar E2 elimination: strong base abstracts beta-H while bromide departs.

templates.name: E2 beta-elimination (HCl)
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Anti-periplanar E2 elimination with chloride leaving group.

templates.name: E2 beta-elimination (HI)
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. E2 elimination with iodide leaving group; highly favored due to weak C-I bond.

templates.name: SN2: alkyl bromide + hydroxide
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Classic SN2 nucleophilic substitution: hydroxide displaces bromide at sp3 carbon with inversion of configuration. Nucleophile left unmapped in product to avoid charge inheritance issues.

templates.name: SN2: alkyl chloride + hydroxide
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. SN2 with hydroxide on chloride substrate.

templates.name: Hydrolysis: alkyl bromide + water
templates.provenance: Adapted from Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Net product of SN1/SN2 hydrolysis. Proton transfer from oxonium intermediate is implicit; net product is the alcohol.

templates.name: Hydrolysis: alkyl chloride + water
templates.provenance: Adapted from Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Net product of SN1/SN2 hydrolysis with chloride leaving group.

templates.name: Finkelstein reaction (Br -> I)
templates.provenance: Finkelstein, H. Ber. Dtsch. Chem. Ges. 1910, 43, 1528. Halide metathesis driven by NaI precipitation. SMARTS adapted from Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098.

templates.name: Finkelstein reaction (Cl -> I)
templates.provenance: Finkelstein, H. Ber. Dtsch. Chem. Ges. 1910, 43, 1528. Halide exchange from chloride. SMARTS from Hartenfeller M. et al. 2011.

templates.name: Williamson ether synthesis (bromide + alkoxide)
templates.provenance: Williamson, A.W. J. Chem. Soc. 1852, 4, 229. SN2 of alkoxide on alkyl bromide to form ether. O left unmapped in product to avoid charge inheritance; electrophilic C (:1) and alkoxide C (:3) are both mapped.

templates.name: Williamson ether synthesis (chloride + alkoxide)
templates.provenance: Williamson, A.W. J. Chem. Soc. 1852, 4, 229. SN2 of alkoxide on alkyl chloride. SMARTS adapted from Hartenfeller M. et al. 2011.

templates.name: Enolate protonation (protic workup)
templates.provenance: Standard enolate quench with protic solvent. Chemistry: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. 1-reactant template (protic condition gates when it fires on enolate intermediates); :2 unmapped in product to add fresh neutral carbonyl O.

templates.name: Halide exchange (Br -> Cl)
templates.provenance: Adapted from Finkelstein-type halide metathesis. Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Thermodynamically less favorable than Br->I (Keq < 1 in most solvents) but possible under forcing conditions with NaCl.

templates.name: N-alkylation: alkyl bromide + ammonia
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. N-alkylation producing ammonium salt; proton transfer gives amine.

templates.name: N-alkylation: alkyl chloride + ammonia
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. N-alkylation of an alkyl chloride with ammonia.

templates.name: Ammonium proton transfer (excess NH3) → primary amine
templates.provenance: Completes the Hartenfeller N-alkylation: excess ammonia deprotonates the alkylammonium salt to the neutral primary amine.

templates.name: Carbonyl gem-diol formation (hydration)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Reversible nucleophilic addition of water to carbonyl to give gem-diol. Equilibrium strongly disfavored for ketones (Keq << 1) but thermodynamically accessible for aldehydes. Restricted to aldehyde/ketone carbonyls — acid/ester/amide carbonyls do not form gem-diols.

templates.name: α-Alkylation: enolate + alkyl bromide
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. SN2 C-alkylation: enolate anion (produced by kinetic_enolate template) acts as carbon nucleophile attacking an alkyl bromide from the molecule pool. Produces alpha-alkylated carbonyl compound with C-C bond formation. Both reactants come from the synthesis pool, not the reagent list — this is a convergent coupling step.

templates.name: α-Alkylation: enolate + alkyl chloride
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Same as alpha_alkylation_br but on alkyl chloride electrophile. Less reactive than bromide but still viable under forcing conditions with a stabilized enolate nucleophile.

templates.name: Terminal alkyne deprotonation (acetylide formation)
templates.provenance: Clayden, J. 'Organic Chemistry' 2nd ed. Strong bases (LDA, t-BuOK, NaNH2) deprotonate terminal alkynes (pKa ~25) to give acetylide anions, which are strong carbon nucleophiles for SN2 on primary alkyl halides.

templates.name: Acetylide SN2: acetylide + primary alkyl bromide
templates.provenance: Clayden, J. 'Organic Chemistry' 2nd ed. Acetylide anion (from acetylide_deprotonation) performs SN2 on a primary or methyl alkyl bromide ([CX4;H2,H3]) to form an internal alkyne with C-C bond formation. Secondary/tertiary halides are excluded ([H0,H1]) because SN2 is not viable there.

templates.name: Acetylide SN2: acetylide + primary alkyl chloride
templates.provenance: Clayden, J. 'Organic Chemistry' 2nd ed. Same as acetylide_alkylation_br but on primary alkyl chloride. Less reactive than bromide but viable with the highly nucleophilic acetylide. Primary/methyl restriction enforced.

templates.name: Alcohol deprotonation (alkoxide formation)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Strong bases (NaH, NaOEt, t-BuOK) deprotonate alcohols (pKa ~16-18) to give alkoxide anions. Prerequisite for Williamson ether synthesis when the alkoxide comes from within the synthesis pool rather than from the reagent list.

templates.name: Williamson ether (pool-pool): alkoxide + primary alkyl bromide
templates.provenance: Williamson, A.W. J. Chem. Soc. 1852, 4, 229. Pool-pool variant: alkoxide generated from alcohol_deprotonation attacks a primary/methyl alkyl bromide from the synthesis pool. O- (unmapped in reactant) is consumed; a fresh neutral ether O is created in the product, avoiding charge inheritance. Primary halide restriction prevents E2 competition.

templates.name: Williamson ether (pool-pool): alkoxide + primary alkyl chloride
templates.provenance: Williamson, A.W. J. Chem. Soc. 1852, 4, 229. Same as williamson_coupling_br but on primary alkyl chloride. Less reactive than bromide but viable with alkoxide nucleophile.

templates.name: Grignard addition: RMgX + aldehyde → secondary alcohol
templates.provenance: Grignard, V. C. R. Acad. Sci. 1900, 130, 1322. The Grignard carbanion (C:1, from RMgX provided as starting material) performs 1,2-addition to an aldehyde carbonyl. Mg and X are unmapped and deleted in the product (simulates aqueous workup). Net: C=O → C-OH with new C-C bond; secondary alcohol. [CX3H:2] restricts to aldehydes (1 H on carbonyl C); [OX1:3] ensures the carbonyl O.

templates.name: Grignard addition: RMgX + ketone → tertiary alcohol
templates.provenance: Grignard, V. C. R. Acad. Sci. 1900, 130, 1322. Same mechanism as grignard_aldehyde but on a disubstituted ketone. [CX3H0:2] requires 0 H on carbonyl C (distinguishes ketone from aldehyde). ([C])[C] flanking constraint ensures both substituents are carbons, excluding esters (one O neighbor) and amides (N neighbor). Product is a tertiary alcohol.

templates.name: Grignard addition: RMgX + formaldehyde → primary alcohol
templates.provenance: Grignard, V. C. R. Acad. Sci. 1900, 130, 1322. Grignard addition to formaldehyde (the only carbonyl with 2 H's on C, [CX3H2:2]) gives a primary alcohol after workup. Product has one more carbon than the Grignard R group: RMgX + HCHO → RCH2OH.

templates.name: NaBH4 reduction: aldehyde → primary alcohol
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. NaBH4 delivers hydride to the carbonyl carbon of an aldehyde; aqueous workup gives the primary alcohol. Net: RCHO → RCH2OH.

templates.name: NaBH4 reduction: ketone → secondary alcohol
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. NaBH4 reduces a ketone to a secondary alcohol via 1,2-hydride delivery. Net: RCOR' → RCHOHR'. Carbon flanks are mapped (grignard_ketone pattern) so the carbonyl must sit between two carbons — esters, acids, and amides no longer match (NaBH4 does not reduce them).

templates.name: LiAlH4 reduction: aldehyde → primary alcohol
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. LiAlH4 is a more powerful reducing agent than NaBH4; reduces aldehydes to primary alcohols.

templates.name: LiAlH4 reduction: ketone → secondary alcohol
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. LiAlH4 reduces ketones to secondary alcohols. Carbon flanks mapped so acids/esters route through their own dedicated templates instead of double-firing here.

templates.name: LiAlH4 reduction: carboxylic acid → primary alcohol
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. LiAlH4 (but not NaBH4) reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols. Net: RCOOH → RCH2OH.

templates.name: HBr addition: terminal alkene → secondary bromide (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Electrophilic HBr addition to CH2=CHR. Markovnikov: proton to terminal CH2 (→ CH3), Br to internal C (→ secondary bromide).

templates.name: HBr addition: trisubstituted alkene → tertiary bromide (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HBr addition to CHR=CR'R''. Markovnikov: Br goes to more substituted C (→ tertiary bromide).

templates.name: HCl addition: terminal alkene → secondary chloride (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Electrophilic HCl addition to CH2=CHR with Markovnikov regiochemistry.

templates.name: HCl addition: trisubstituted alkene → tertiary chloride (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HCl Markovnikov addition to trisubstituted alkene.

templates.name: HI addition: terminal alkene → secondary iodide (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HI is the most reactive HX for electrophilic addition; Markovnikov regiochemistry.

templates.name: HI addition: trisubstituted alkene → tertiary iodide (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HI Markovnikov addition to trisubstituted alkene; mirrors the HBr/HCl variants.

templates.name: HBr addition: 1,1-disubstituted alkene → tertiary bromide (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. The textbook Markovnikov case: CH2=CR2 (e.g. isobutylene) + HBr → tertiary bromide. Previously uncovered — the terminal template requires an internal C-H and the disubstituted template requires CHR=.

templates.name: HCl addition: 1,1-disubstituted alkene → tertiary chloride (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HCl Markovnikov addition to a 1,1-disubstituted alkene (CH2=CR2) → tertiary chloride.

templates.name: HI addition: 1,1-disubstituted alkene → tertiary iodide (Markovnikov)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HI Markovnikov addition to a 1,1-disubstituted alkene (CH2=CR2) → tertiary iodide.

templates.name: HBr addition: 1,2-disubstituted alkene → secondary bromide
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HX addition to an internal RCH=CHR' alkene: both carbons are equally substituted, so both regiochemical products form (RunReactants enumerates both atom mappings; unique products are kept).

templates.name: HCl addition: 1,2-disubstituted alkene → secondary chloride
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HCl addition to an internal RCH=CHR' alkene; both regiochemical products enumerated.

templates.name: HI addition: 1,2-disubstituted alkene → secondary iodide
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. HI addition to an internal RCH=CHR' alkene; both regiochemical products enumerated.

templates.name: Br2 addition: alkene → vicinal dibromide
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Electrophilic Br2 addition via bromonium ion; anti addition (stereo not tracked). Net: C=C → C(Br)-C(Br) vicinal dibromide.

templates.name: Cl2 addition: alkene → vicinal dichloride
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Electrophilic Cl2 addition to alkene. Net: C=C → C(Cl)-C(Cl) vicinal dichloride.

templates.name: Carboxylic acid deprotonation → carboxylate
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Carboxylic acids (pKa ~5) are deprotonated by strong bases or hydroxide to give the resonance-stabilized carboxylate anion.

templates.name: Acid-catalyzed dehydration: secondary/tertiary alcohol → alkene
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. E1 dehydration of a secondary or tertiary alcohol under acid catalysis (H2SO4, H3PO4) via carbocation intermediate. Net: -CHOH-CH- → -C=C- + H2O.

templates.name: Aldol addition: enolate + aldehyde → beta-hydroxy carbonyl
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. C-C bond-forming aldol reaction: enolate (from kinetic_enolate) attacks the carbonyl of an aldehyde. Net: C=C-O- + RCHO → C(=O)-CH-CH(OH)R (beta-hydroxy carbonyl).

templates.name: Ester saponification: ester + hydroxide → carboxylate + alcohol
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Base-promoted ester hydrolysis (saponification): hydroxide attacks carbonyl C, alkoxide leaves, gives carboxylate + alcohol. Ester O restricted to non-ring (!R): on a lactone the two disconnected product fragments each duplicate the whole ring remnant, violating mass conservation — lactones use the dedicated ring-opening template.

templates.name: Lactone saponification: cyclic ester + hydroxide → hydroxy-carboxylate
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Ring-opening saponification of a lactone: hydroxide attacks the carbonyl, the ring C-O bond breaks, giving a single open-chain hydroxy-carboxylate. Product atoms grouped as ONE component — writing them as two fragments duplicates the ring remnant into both.

SMARTS authored for Orgo AI and mechanically verified: fires on the documented substrate giving the expected product, and passes all four gates in validate_templates.py (schema, SMARTS well-formedness, condition wiring, atom conservation).

templates.name: Imine hydrolysis: imine + water → carbonyl
templates.provenance: Batch 1 (curriculum expansion). Completes the Grignard/nitrile and imine-condensation routes: the carbonyl oxygen is introduced here at aqueous workup rather than fabricated in the addition step.

templates.name: Aromatic chlorination (Cl2/AlCl3): arene → aryl chloride
templates.provenance: Batch 1 (curriculum expansion). Chlorine drawn from Cl2 so the halogen cannot be conjured.

templates.name: Hemiacetal formation: aldehyde + alcohol → hemiacetal
templates.provenance: Batch 1 (curriculum expansion). Acetal formation is split into its two real steps: a one-equivalent SMARTS that wrote both alkoxy groups duplicated the alcohol's carbons out of nothing. The engine reaches the acetal by chaining.

templates.name: Acetal formation: hemiacetal + alcohol → acetal
templates.provenance: Batch 1 (curriculum expansion). Acetal formation is split into its two real steps: a one-equivalent SMARTS that wrote both alkoxy groups duplicated the alcohol's carbons out of nothing. The engine reaches the acetal by chaining.

templates.name: SOCl2: alcohol → alkyl chloride
templates.provenance: Batch 2 (alcohol activation). Clayden, 'Organic Chemistry' 2nd ed., ch. 15; Carey & Sundberg part B. Thionyl chloride converts an alcohol to the alkyl chloride via the chlorosulfite ester, with SO2 and HCl as byproducts. The reagent side of the SMARTS matches the full S(=O)Cl2 skeleton rather than a bare Cl: _infer_conditions collapses SOCl2, TsCl and HCl to the same 'hcl' tag, so the condition list cannot distinguish them and the skeleton match is what keeps HCl from firing this template. Carries the 'hcl' tag as well as 'chlorinating_agent' so the photo/OSR path — which only ever sees inferred tags — still reaches it.

templates.name: SOCl2: carboxylic acid → acyl chloride
templates.provenance: Batch 2 (alcohol activation). Clayden, 'Organic Chemistry' 2nd ed., ch. 10. The other canonical SOCl2 transform, and the one that feeds the existing acid_chloride_amine / acid_chloride_alcohol / friedel_crafts_acylation templates, so acids now chain through to amides, esters and aryl ketones. [OX2H] on an sp2 carbonyl carbon restricts it to the free acid — esters and amides have no O-H and do not match.

templates.name: PBr3: alcohol → alkyl bromide
templates.provenance: Batch 2 (alcohol activation). Clayden, 'Organic Chemistry' 2nd ed., ch. 15. Phosphorus tribromide converts an alcohol to the alkyl bromide without the carbocation rearrangement that plagues the HBr route. Same skeleton-matching rationale as socl2_alcohol_to_chloride: PBr3 infers the bare 'hbr' tag, so the PX3(Br)(Br)Br match is what separates it from HBr itself.

templates.name: TsCl: alcohol → tosylate
templates.provenance: Batch 2 (alcohol activation). Clayden, 'Organic Chemistry' 2nd ed., ch. 15. Tosylation converts the alcohol's bad leaving group into a good one with retention at carbon (the C-O bond is never broken). The alcohol oxygen is mapped and carried into the product as [O;H0] so RDKit drops its hydrogen; leaving it unconstrained inherits the reactant H count and fails sanitization.
